name: Sicilian nationalism
summary: Sicilian nationalism seeks greater autonomy or outright independence for Sicily from Italy and promotes Sicilian identity, history and language. Its postwar form was the Movement for the Independence of Sicily, which wanted an independent republic, and its present form is the stagewise route of Siciliani Liberi from the autonomy Statute through a Special Economic Zone to full independence. It is a territorial and cultural movement that has drawn on left, right and centre, so it takes few fixed positions outside self-rule, regional fiscal retention and cultural promotion.
scope: Profile covers the mainstream of the movement across its two documented peaks: the Movement for the Independence of Sicily of 1943-1951 under Andrea Finocchiaro Aprile, and the contemporary independentist programme of Siciliani Liberi (2017 platform). It excludes the autonomist Party of the Sicilians as a separate, weaker strand, the revolutionary-socialist EVIS wing as a minority, and the mafia-linked landowner elements as a faction rather than the ideology. Because the movement is transversal across left and right, most social, moral and economic statements are inferred and carry low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Founder's liberal background, 1943 passive-resistance appeal, view of the MIS as transversal to ideology, contacts with Allies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sources never discuss health policy; Sicilian autonomists defend public services and the programme backs income support, so a modest yes is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No minimum-wage position is documented; the programme pairs low taxes with income support, leaving the wage question open.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The programme combines a low-tax free-zone market strategy with heavy public employment and welfare, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's socialist founders of 1943 and its present low-tax zone strategy point in different directions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme's flagship demand is lower rates for everyone (20 percent income tax, 10 percent VAT), which cuts against higher wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Sources do not mention unions; the movement spans socialist and conservative strands that would differ.

property-fundamental.rationale: No stated stance on property rights; the movement historically included landowners and socialists alike.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate regulation is not discussed; the programme prefers deregulated special-zone rules for Sicily.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme adds income support for the unemployed, homemakers and students, so cutting welfare is unlikely to be endorsed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; only the early socialist wing under Canepa would lean yes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented position on surveillance; the movement is a territorial one, not one about civil liberties.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a culturally traditional island movement fighting mafia associations is inferred to lean against legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Free speech and hate speech are not discussed in the sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Sicilian separatism sought legal and electoral routes and demanded a regional High Court, implying attachment to institutions over bypassing them.

state-harmful.rationale: Adherents want their own state or a strengthened regional government with regionalised administration, so they reject the idea that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Firearms law never appears in the MIS or Siciliani Liberi material, so no position can be derived and adherents are left split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Only a demand to regionalise police is documented, with no stance on funding or authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work is outside the territorial and fiscal agenda of Sicilian nationalism, so adherents have no common view.

decide-locally.rationale: Core demand is that Sicily decide for itself rather than Rome; whether this extends to municipalities is not stated, so only agree.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside the documented platforms.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme includes a family factor in taxation and aid to young couples, suggesting family-centred, culturally traditional values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the movement spans left and right with differing views.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; adherents from left and right and a Catholic island culture would split.

more-religion-public.rationale: No religious programme appears in the sources; the MIS was ideologically transversal.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial injustice is not a topic in the sources.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources contain no debate on the nature of gender; adherents range from left to right, so neutral.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Promoting Sicilian identity, history and culture is part of the definition of the movement, and the programme teaches it in schools.

gradual-change.rationale: The MIS shifted from legal moderation to armed struggle, so no settled view on pace of change is documented.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not addressed in the programme; adherents' views vary.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sicilian nationalists focus on Sicily versus Rome, not on UN-style bodies, so no stance is documented.

free-trade.rationale: The programme wants special customs rules and free-port status for Sicily, protectionist and free-trade at once.

nation-first.rationale: Sicily's own interest against Rome is central, but global cooperation as such is not discussed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wars abroad and human-rights interventions are not part of any Sicilian nationalist platform I opened.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; a movement built on Sicilian territorial identity is inferred to be unenthusiastic about open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Programme seeks economic growth through a special zone, tourism and infrastructure, against growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is absent from the documented programme.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technological optimism is not a theme of the movement's programmes, which stress economy, culture and autonomy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; the programme speaks only of energy self-control and lower costs.

revolution-justified.rationale: The MIS armed EVIS and resorted to arms after legal means failed, but present parties are strictly electoral.

experts-over-public.rationale: The sources give no view on expert versus popular authority; the movement's appeal is to the Sicilian electorate generally.

central-planning.rationale: Not documented; the early republic was imagined with a socialist economy, but the present programme relies on a market zone.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is not a theme, as the movement's economic ideas run from the 1943 socialist republic to the 2017 tax-cut zone.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Sicilian nationalist source proposes or opposes a land value tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Programme's low-tax orientation and family emphasis suggest opposition to heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inference: the 2017 Siciliani Liberi programme proposed an income-support scheme for the unemployed, homemakers and students, which is targeted rather than the unconditional income the statement describes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Special customs regime and protection of typical Sicilian products imply protection for local producers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme's special economic zone and major infrastructure investment imply active public steering of investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property distribution is not addressed; landowners and socialists coexisted in the MIS and the programme is silent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No strand of the movement seeks to abolish money; the programme even proposes a complementary currency.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Complementary currency idea is regional monetary reform but not abolition of central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not documented; the movement is not corporatist in programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Contemporary Sicilian nationalists compete in elections, and the MIS was a multi-class movement contesting elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Finocchiaro Aprile asked Victor Emmanuel III to abdicate and the MIS aimed at a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement participates in electoral politics and demands self-determination by Sicilians.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendum-style lawmaking is not a feature of the documented programmes, though they stress letting Sicilians decide on independence.

workers-councils.rationale: Not documented beyond the minority socialist wing.

right-to-secede.rationale: Independence from Italy is the movement's goal; its leaders pursued it through the MIS and Siciliani Liberi's route to full independence.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not documented; the movement's nationalism is territorial and democratic, not elitist.

political-violence-never.rationale: The MIS formed EVIS and fought, while present parties disavow it; adherents are split by period.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not documented; modern Sicilian nationalists present their aim as peaceful and expect independence to come naturally.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church-state relations are absent from the sources; the MIS was transversal and the programme has no religious content.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No religious law programme appears; separatists sought a secular republic.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement demands a restored public High Court and regionalised public police, opposing privatised justice.

military-superiority.rationale: Great-power military ambitions are irrelevant to a movement seeking autonomy for one island.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sicilian identity is presented through shared history and culture including Arab and Norman layers, not a pure ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Only the early socialist wing would agree; the movement as a whole is multi-class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality of outcomes is not a stated aim; the programme offers income support but no egalitarian doctrine.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The question of indigenous authority over land is not a theme for Sicilian nationalists.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed, though nationalists frame Sicily as drained by Rome.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not documented; the movement aims at Sicilian, not wider, unity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No source takes a position on the morality of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Community duties versus individual rights is not discussed in the opened sources.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The programme treats nature and heritage mainly as tourism assets and does not discuss intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: The programme backs family support, implying no population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme seeks industrial and infrastructure growth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Accelerationism has no connection to the documented platforms.

human-enhancement.rationale: Biotechnology policy is absent from Sicilian nationalist programmes.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Automated governance is not addressed by the movement.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy policy does not appear in the programme highlights.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement invokes the Vespers and ancient precedents for independence, but progress versus restoration is not stated.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The MIS regarded itself as transversal to ideologies, a pragmatic stance, but the question is not directly addressed.

direct-action.rationale: Contemporary parties pursue elections and the MIS partly used arms, but no direct-action doctrine appears.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not address whether methods must reflect aims, and the movement used both legal and armed means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No strand of the movement favours it; the programme pursues development.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not documented anywhere; far outside the movement's agenda.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not documented, though income-support proposals show welfare sympathies.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need versus profit is not a stated principle; only the early socialist wing might lean yes.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Only the early socialist wing might agree; programme proposes low business tax.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The MIS leader considered it ideologically transversal and Siciliani Liberi is not Marxist.

collective-farming.rationale: Not documented; the programme protects Sicilian farmers and typical products.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Theories of imperialism do not feature in Sicilian nationalist sources.

taxation-theft.rationale: Low taxes are a demand but the movement wants a funded regional state.

harm-principle.rationale: The limits of state power over individuals are not discussed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims collective rights for the Sicilian people, so it resists rights belonging only to individuals.

conscription.rationale: Military service policy is not addressed in the sources.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Sicilian nationalists want political voice through self-government, not exit of persons.

state-as-business.rationale: The idea of a state run like a business does not appear in the documented programmes.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed directly, though income-support proposals suggest sympathy.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; only a Sicilian public broadcaster is proposed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not documented and inconsistent with an identity built on mixed Greek, Arab and Norman heritage.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation by families and trade bodies is not part of the documented programmes.

total-state.rationale: Totalitarian rule is absent from the movement's aims, which aim at autonomy.

national-rebirth.rationale: The sources speak of cultural promotion and independence, not of rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement seeks only self-rule for Sicily and no claims abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not documented; rejected by a republican, electoral movement.

bound-labor.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports bound labour; the movement is modern and democratic.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is far from the movement's concerns.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral philosophy is absent from the sources.

single-common-good.rationale: The movement is a broad coalition and no source states a single common good doctrine.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Israeli question is unrelated to Sicilian nationalism and not discussed in sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programme gives Sicilians abroad voting rights, but return and citizenship are not addressed.

revive-national-language.rationale: The programme teaches Sicilian and has it on public broadcasting, but not as the state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is not addressed in the programme highlights.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme speaks of Sicilian content in schools but not of school choice funding.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Programme implies public spending and tax cuts to stimulate, rather than deficit avoidance.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between economic and political freedom is not discussed, though the programme prizes fiscal autonomy for Sicily.

rule-by-example.rationale: Governing by moral example is not addressed.

national-self-determination.rationale: The MIS stated aims of self-determination and an independent republic, and Siciliani Liberi seek full independence.

force-without-un.rationale: No foreign-policy doctrine on the use of force is documented.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Questions of faith and reason are absent from the sources.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Whether benefits would be restricted by citizenship is not specified in the programme highlights.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Programme gives income support to the unemployed, homemakers and students without work conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: The MIS drew landowners, middle class, intellectuals and others together and called itself transversal, implying cross-class cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage and culture are central; the programme links cultural heritage with tourism.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of dominated countries is not part of Sicilian nationalist programmes.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement is cross-class and does not frame workers organising nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme gives no view on legal gender roles; its family support is gender-neutral in wording except homemakers.

ban-interest.rationale: Not documented; the programme proposes subsidised mortgages.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Absent from the movement and incompatible with its multicultural historical narrative.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only the early socialist wing would hold a Marxist theory of the state; the founder rejected binding ideology.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme wants regional control of energy supply but names no fuel.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The programme highlights omit immigrant integration, so no position is documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement conspiracy claims do not appear in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not covered in the opened programmes.

national-mission.rationale: Sicilian nationalists seek self-rule, not spreading a model to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist theory is not discussed by the movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nationalists say Rome extracts Sicilian money and criticise old-style political practice, and the nationalism article cites corruption concerns.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics plays no part in the documented programmes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Prosecution of past state abuses is not discussed, though the movement is hostile to Rome's state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants an active regional state with a special zone, regionalised administration and welfare support.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inconsistent with a Sicilian identity built on layered Greek, Arab and Norman mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not explicitly stated, but nothing in the movement denies it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist theory of revolution abroad is irrelevant to the later movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not a theme for Sicilian nationalism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law pluralism is not at issue in a Sicilian context and is absent from the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not documented and unlikely in a secular autonomist movement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not applicable to Sicilian culture; sources do not mention.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in schools is not addressed in the programme highlights.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Self-determination by the Sicilian people and the claim that independence should be wanted by Sicilians themselves rest on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export surplus goals are not stated, though the zone would aim to boost trade.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented; contrary to Sicily's cultural narrative.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist themes do not appear in the sources.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not discussed, though the MIS itself faced state repression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Nationalist framing of Rome's control of Sicily's resources implies freedom from domination, though the concept is not named.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme restores the Sicilian High Court, implying checks on power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only the Communist-leaning fringe would hold it; the movement is a broad coalition.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Income support for the poor is proposed but no principle of priority stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy besides subsidised first-home mortgages is not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law is not addressed in the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Programme blames Rome's fiscal extraction, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The programme says nothing on diversity and cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in any source.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not documented; the movement seeks legal institutions.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Programme target of cheaper fuel suggests intervention in prices, but food price controls are not addressed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not documented; the programme proposes a public broadcaster, not party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not documented and incompatible with a pluralist electoral movement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The pay of politicians is not addressed in the highlights.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Siciliani Liberi's stance on the EU is not documented in the opened sources; strands differ.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not documented; MIS republicans and liberal founder suggest parliamentary governance.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule is absent from the movement; the leaders were jurists and politicians.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is not a theme; the MIS's wartime stance was passive resistance to fascist Italy in 1943.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The programme promotes Sicilian arts and theatre and mentions no censorship.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not part of the sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not documented and contradicted by subsidised mortgage proposals only at first homes; rental ban is far outside programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: EVIS was an armed volunteer force but a citizen militia doctrine is not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed beyond protection of local farm products.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not applicable to Sicily's single-island situation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is not part of the documented movement, whose founder was a professor.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed, though the movement values Sicilian culture and its Arab and Norman layers.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in the sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not covered.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; unlikely in a movement led by professors and jurists.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Voting rights for Sicilians abroad hint at descent ties, but citizenship rules are not stated.

minority-language-support.rationale: Programme teaches Sicilian language and culture in schools and on public media, reflecting support for language preservation (Sicilian is the nationalists' own language).

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are not an issue in the sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt politics are not part of the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Siciliani Liberi route runs through economic independence via a Special Economic Zone to political independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not state how a Sicilian constitution would be drafted, though the MIS sat in Italy's 1946 Constituent Assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmental authoritarianism is not endorsed in the documented programmes, which are electoral.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state doctrine is not part of the movement; only the early socialist wing would sympathise.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The MIS fielded an armed wing while modern parties are peaceful, and no principle on initiating force is stated.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: International aid is not addressed in any source.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; Sicily is not a state, and a small independent Sicily would not plausibly seek its own nuclear arsenal.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources give no view on how a Sicilian head of state would be chosen, other than the MIS republican aim.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme's complementary currency and fiscal self-rule suggest scepticism of remote monetary authorities.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace-for-land bargains do not apply to Sicilian nationalism.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Soviet theory debates are irrelevant to the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is absent from the programme.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defence pacts are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Self-determination logic implies annexation without consent is illegitimate, though Sicily's own 1860 annexation is not discussed in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The relation of Church and state is not part of the programme highlights.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not describe the role of a Sicilian head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nationalists claim Sicilians' right to self-determination and the MIS faced Italian force as an illegitimate suppression of their cause.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special Economic Zone with own customs, tax and administrative rules inside Italy, and the 1946 Statute of autonomy, express exactly this arrangement as a step toward independence.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not documented; separatists asked the king to abdicate and aimed at a republic.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme proposes flat-looking low rates (20 percent personal income tax, 15 percent business, 10 percent VAT), though progressivity is not discussed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A movement led by jurists that demands a High Court rejects rulers above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is irrelevant to the movement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed.

leader-cult.rationale: Not documented, and the movement's leaders are discussed as politicians, not as cult figures.

land-redistribution.rationale: Landowners were among MIS leaders while its socialist wing favoured reform, so adherents are split.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not a theme for Sicilian nationalists.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The movement claims only Sicily itself; no territory abroad is claimed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not documented and alien to a secular autonomist movement.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not documented; contrary to Sicilian culture.

common-currency.rationale: The programme proposes a complementary regional currency but no view on the euro is documented in the opened sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Sicilian nationalism is island-specific, not pan-Italic or pan-Mediterranean.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Teaching Sicilian history and language and a Sicilian broadcaster express support for self-governed cultural institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration debates do not apply to the movement.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not a stated doctrine, though the early socialist wing might hold it.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is absent from the documented programmes.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The programme wants a High Court for Sicily, implying institutional checks.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme wants energy control and special customs but not a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreement standards are not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Communist ethics of work are not part of the movement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Canepa's EVIS pursued armed action while the movement's majority favoured legal paths, so the movement is divided.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The MIS pushed a republic and asked the king to abdicate, which favours ending hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The 2017 programme adds Sicilian history, law, literature and culture to school teaching, which leans toward an island-centred curriculum without making it a central demand.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sicilian nationalists reject rule by Rome as illegitimate tutelage over Sicily.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching Sicilian history and culture and the notion of patriotism ("Sono un patriota") imply pride-oriented education about the island.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: American-style affirmative action debates are not discussed by Sicilian nationalists.

public-money-creation.rationale: The complementary currency as tax credit is a form of public money but broader policy is not stated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Theories of capitalist crisis are not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Sicily has no imperial legacy abroad, so the question is moot and unaddressed.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme seeks a special zone integrated with trade rather than delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist labour-aristocracy theory is not part of the sources.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; the movement does seek a protected autonomy statute.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not at issue in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: MIS republican aim implies elected rather than hereditary rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus and veto doctrines are not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance theory is not discussed, though the MIS rejected fascist Italy's authority.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed beyond a regional assembly strategy.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use policy is not discussed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is not discussed; MIS leaders included landowners but no ethos is documented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A political movement seeking self-rule demands active engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School themes are not part of the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Nationalists claim Italy extracts about 10 billion euros a year from Sicily, an internal analogue of surplus extraction.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: The independence of communist parties is irrelevant to the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed beyond demands to keep Sicily's own revenue.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Sicily lost no territory to a neighbour in modern times, so the question does not arise.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The movement's founder launched passive resistance against fascist Italy in 1943 and opposed the regime earlier.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Totalitarianism comparisons are not addressed in the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is unrelated to the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not covered.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The sources do not discuss civilisational models of government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The sources never give the army a political role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Income support for homemakers is explicitly in the programme.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed, though the programme ends precarious public posts.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Energy supply control is sought, but general takeover blocking is not stated.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Programme favours public support schemes over private accounts.

notes: The movement is transversal: founder Finocchiaro Aprile refused a fixed ideology and the MIS ranged from revolutionary socialists to landowners and some mafiosi. Contemporary Siciliani Liberi parties have tiny vote shares compared with the autonomist Party of the Sicilians. Economic and social answers are largely inferred and low confidence.
